implementation_notes: With a messaging library the package is already a type: ZeroMQ delivers multipart messages atomically, the first frame conventionally holds the header/envelope (routing id, command, metadata) and the following frames carry the body, with zmq::message_t representing one frame, the 'more' bit (zmq::send_flags::sndmore) chaining frames into one message, and zmq_addon.hpp supplying zmq::multipart_t plus send_multipart/recv_multipart to build and parse header+body packages. The other packaged form in C++ is RPC-shaped: gRPC keeps per-call metadata (headers) beside a typed protobuf message (body) and the framework transports both as one unit. Hand-rolling a header struct plus a serialized body over a raw socket remains justified when a foreign wire format is mandated or the library may not be linked.
pitfalls: The header/body split is a convention, not a type: a consumer that always treats frame 0 as a header mis-parses single-frame messages, so write the framing convention down.
zmq::message_t(buffer, size) copies, while the free-function overload takes ownership of the buffer; mixing the two with stack buffers or string temporaries is a classic lifetime bug.
For the gRPC form, metadata is bounded by the transport's metadata size limit and cannot carry payload data - oversized metadata fails the call, and large payloads belong in the message body.
